images.filename: 2016 One World Observatory view southsoutheast towards Governors Island.jpg
images.caption: A view south-southeast of Governors Island from the One World Observatory at One World Trade Center, Manhattan, New York City. Off the tip of the island, at the left, can be seen the white ventilation building for the Brooklyn-Battery Tunnel. Buttermilk Channel runs between the island and Brooklyn, and Gowanus Bay can be seen beyond that on the left. In the background, can be seen the Verrazano-Narrows Bridge across the Narrows between Staten Island and Brooklyn, with Lower New York Bay and the Atlantic Ocean beyond that.
images.alt: A view south-southeast of Governors Island from the One World Observatory at One World Trade Center, Manhattan, New York City. Off the tip of the island, at the left, can be seen the white ventilation building for the Brooklyn-Battery Tunnel. Buttermilk Channel runs between the island and Brooklyn, and Gowanus Bay can be seen beyond that on the left. In the background, can be seen the Verrazano-Narrows Bridge across the Narrows between Staten Island and Brooklyn, with Lower New York Bay and the Atlantic Ocean beyond that.

images.filename: 2016 One World Observatory view southsouthwest towards Verrazano-Narrows Bridge.jpg
images.caption: A view south-southwest towards the Verrazano-Narrows Bridge from the One World Observatory at One World Trade Center, Manhattan, New York City.  The bridge is over the Narrows seperating Lower New York Bay from Upper New York Bay (also known as New York Harbor), which can be seen in the foreground. On the right of the bridge is Staten Island, and on the left is Brooklyn.  A tip of Governors Island can be seen in the left foreground.
images.alt: A view south-southwest towards the Verrazano-Narrows Bridge from the One World Observatory at One World Trade Center, Manhattan, New York City.  The bridge is over the Narrows seperating Lower New York Bay from Upper New York Bay (also known as New York Harbor), which can be seen in the foreground. On the right of the bridge is Staten Island, and on the left is Brooklyn.  A tip of Governors Island can be seen in the left foreground.
